items.safeture-regional-0: Reconsider travel to the West Bank until further notice due to ongoing heightened tensions and frequent Israel’s military operations. Violence has increased between Israel Defence Forces (IDF), Israeli settlers and Palestinians since the conflict in Gaza began on 7 October 2023, with increased Israeli raids, arrests, settler attacks and land seizures. Further lockdowns, incursions, violent settler attacks and Israeli raids, prompting unrest and violence, are certain in the near-term. …

items.safeture-regional-93: Defer non-essential travel to southern Lebanon in the near-term due to ongoing tensions between Hezbollah and Israel, following joint Israeli-United States strikes on Iran and Iranian retaliatory attacks across the region since the end of February. On 17 April, a 10-day ceasefire between the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) and Hezbollah came into effect in Lebanon, which was subsequently extended by three-weeks on 23 April and by 45 days on 15 May; a renewed ceasefire commitment was made on 19 June. The IDF warned residents not to attempt to return to their homes and continue to occupy a 10km (6.2 mi) buffer zone south of the Litani River. The recent escalation comes after the November 2024 ceasefire, which ended nearly 14 months of hostilities, collapsed and cross-border attacks resumed, with Israeli officials authorising ground troops to advance and seize additional territory. While Beirut-Rafic Hariri International Airport (BEY/OLBA) remains operational, persistent flight suspensions and disruptions continue. …
